items.title: Al Gallodoro Interview, 1966-05-10
items.q: Dr. Frank Black was a big conductor. He says, Al, you're playing these a tone too high.

ctx.x: I think, you know, you had so many years of experience with Paul Whiteman, starting with Toscanini. Right. Why don't you people ask some questions? He has some terrific stories. We just came off of a radio show with Roy Roberts on WSMB, what, an hour or two ago? Oh, 11 to 1131. You know, the nut to nut and stuff sort of thing. And yesterday we were on WWL. And Mr. Gavro has some marvelous things, stories that will help you even musically. Yes. Sure. So why don't you fire away? Start with the Paul Whiteman area if…

Well, I suppose I'll tell them about the Toscanini incident. Yeah, come on. Well, you've heard of Paul LaValle, the band leader, Paul LaValle. Well, I was working an ice show. Sonya Henney and Arthur Works opened up this ice show. They weren't in the show. Like the shows that you see now on tour, the ice shows, Holiday on the Ice and so forth. All right. Well, we opened the original. And Paul LaValle at that time was at NBC. And he says, Al, he says, how would you like to go with Toscanini? I said, gee, I don't…
One today in the back, wait a minute.

items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: And anyway I had my clarinet and my bass clarinet on the stage and who is up there? Toscanini. Dr. Frank Black.

ctx.x: Or 30. I had turned 30 and that’s why. And then I had four children at the time. And oh God, well anyway Sal Francella, who was my sidekick in the Whiteman band, he was also from New Orleans and we knew each other as young boys from New Orleans. He called me or something, he sent a telegram, he says, “I’m going into an ice show, and I can get you in.” And I accepted it. That was October of 1940. “It Happens on Ice” at the old Center Theater. Well now, but they tore it down, anyway, I did that for a couple of…
And your family was already — you already had a place in New York?
